question:
Two metal cathodes made of Platinum and Cesium are being considered for an electron source based on **field emission** (electrons are pulled out of the metal by applying a very strong external electric field).

Given that the work functions are $\phi_{0,P}=5.65\,\text{eV}$ for Platinum and $\phi_{0,Cs}=2.14\,\text{eV}$ for Cesium, and assuming both cathodes have **identical geometry and surface condition** (so only material property matters), analyze how the work function affects the minimum external electric field required to start emission.

Hence, determine which metal would require a **stronger** electric field to initiate field emission and justify the reason.

options.A: Cesium requires a stronger field because its lower work function causes electron crowding that opposes emission
options.B: Platinum requires a stronger field because a higher work function means electrons are more strongly bound at the surface, so a stronger external field is needed to pull them out
options.C: Both require the same field because field emission depends only on the shape/geometry of the cathode and not on the work function
options.D: Cesium requires a stronger field because alkali metals resist losing electrons in vacuum due to chemical reactivity
